purpose: Constrain PTGAE output so written content remains navigable and understandable without deleting necessary technical meaning.

headings: Use headings that name the section's actual subject or task.
Keep heading levels structurally nested; do not use heading level only for visual size.
Avoid headings whose only content is generic words such as Overview, Information, or Notes when a concrete label is available.
links: Use link text that identifies the destination or action without relying on surrounding prose.
Do not use bare 'click here' or 'learn more' when the destination can be named.
altText: Describe the image information needed for the consuming context.
Do not restate a filename, asset ID, decorative caption, or nearby prose as alt text.
Mark decorative images as decorative through the target platform instead of inventing explanatory text.
structure: Use lists for real enumerations, sequences, options, requirements, or checklists; do not turn every paragraph into bullets.
Prefer short paragraphs when long dependency chains make the relation between claims hard to follow.
Keep labels, units, dates, states, and actions explicit in tables and status displays.
plainLanguage: Use the ordinary word when it preserves the technical meaning.
Introduce a required specialist term directly and define it where the audience cannot be expected to know it.
Do not use a reading-level score as a universal quality target.

exceptions: Code, formulas, identifiers, formal notation, quoted source, and required legal/technical terms keep their exact surface unless their owning domain changes them.
Target-language localization follows the target language's conventions rather than English accessibility heuristics that do not transfer.
